# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — title + description (description contains the ACs and the Key Files
   section). The per-path git components (committed HEAD blob hashes, working-tree
   state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are **removed** from the fingerprint
   — **no git calls in the computation** (`_resolve_touched_files` /
   `_compute_path_fingerprints` are no longer used by the fingerprint).
   *(PENDING producer decision — see OPEN QUESTION in Appendix.)*
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate
   a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test:
   fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored
   audit — **including changes to files the item itself touched** (stricter than
   the current per-touched-path formula). Regression test: fingerprint is stable
   across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences and
   across touched-file edits.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files
   section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing
   description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do
   **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content). This
   also removes the current comment-recorded-commit-hash contribution to the
   touched set (SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L) — the fingerprint must not depend on comments.
6. **Migration of legacy reports:** reports persisted before this change carry
   fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formulas that cannot be recomputed.
   Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`)
   so legacy/unversioned lines are distinguishable; legacy/unversioned reports
   fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt +
   `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`, plus the persist-write tolerance) — **no
   silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the
   one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after
   the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: after the simplification, remove the fingerprints-only
   git machinery no longer referenced elsewhere (verify each of
   `_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` — those still used by
   the file-scope manifest and Phase 2 remain). `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
   (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ) is **already removed**; `_resolve_audited_head` stays
   (still used by green-run attestation).
8. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate
   section, currently ~lines 248-318/579-594/699/816), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
   (~lines 42/182-186/204-210), and the code docstrings on
   `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` /
   `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. All fingerprint call sites that must keep
   working with the simplified formula: `_check_audit_freshness` (item gate),
   `_get_child_audit_verdict` + `_child_content_changed` (child reuse, LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR),
   `cmd_check_freshness` (read-only probe, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI),
   `_run_remediation_loop` (ruff-config re-hash), `_phase_fetch_and_cq`,
   `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children`, `_phase_children` (child audit persistence).
   Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is
  reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the
  gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make
  any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still
  short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved); the read-only
  `check-freshness` probe and `isAuditFresh` (ship, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI) keep
  working.
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls
  through to a full re-audit (existing behaviour).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse uses the same fingerprint — it must keep
  working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2412) — payload =
    `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` (per-touched-path, SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P).
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~1950) — content gate primary; time gate
    (60 s + persist-write tolerance ~30 s) floor for fingerprint-less legacy
    reports; persistence-write tolerance covers the runner's own writes
    (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
  - `_extract_content_fingerprint` (line ~2073) — parses the unversioned line.
  - `_resolve_touched_files` (line ~2213), `_compute_path_fingerprints`
    (line ~2336) — the per-touched-path git machinery this item's strict rule
    removes from the fingerprint (verify remaining uses: file-scope manifest at
    ~5224/7964/10897).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line ~1112,
    unversioned); embedded at ~5721/5747/6172 (persist) + re-extracted by the gate.
  - Call sites of the fingerprint: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020),
    `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_child_content_changed` (~7009),
    `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120), `_phase_gate` (~9466),
    `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357),
    `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11380/11516/11918).
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` — **already removed** (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ
    component replaced by per-path state); `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) stays.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — tests split across files; fingerprint/freshness coverage
  lives mainly in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (1336 lines:
  `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~190, `TestContentFreshnessGate` ~348 — incl.
  `test_fingerprint_payload_keys_exclude_global_head`, touched-file invalidation
  tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`, comment-hash tests) and
  `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`. Some existing tests assert the
  per-touched-path invalidation behaviour that this item reverses
  (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` /
  `..._dirty` / `..._staged`, tool-artefact invalidation, comment-contribution
  tests, `test_child_content_changed_fresh_survives_unrelated_head_movement` —
  these must be updated to the new rule).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section ~lines 248-254
  (content gate + time gate + fail-open), 292/309-318 (child reuse), 579/594
  (inherited pass / child reuse), 699/816 (Phase 2 child reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary ~lines 42, 182-186, 204-210.
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side
  `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based
  `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this;
  covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog). The ship-side
  `isAuditFresh` consumption is SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI (done) and stays in scope
  only as a consumer that must keep working.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`
  (simplify to item-data-only), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_extract_content_fingerprint`
  (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, dead-git-
  machinery removal, docstrings
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — update
  fingerprint/freshness tests to the new rule
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary lines

## Related work

- `SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P` — Audit freshness: re-audit only when files touched by
  the work item changed (**done**, 2026-09-28) — implemented the per-touched-path
  formula currently in the code; this item's strict rule goes further (item-data-
  only, zero git). **The original observed failure is already fixed by this item.**
- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content
  fingerprint (**done**, not in_review as the original brief stated) — the
  whole-repo working-tree component this item's rule REMOVES (superseded; the
  per-path state it inspired is also removed by this strict rule).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (**done**) —
  introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L` — Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments
  (**done**, 2026-10-21) — comment-recorded commit hashes feed the touched set;
  this item's rule removes the comment dependency (AC5).
- `SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI` — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (**done**) — read-only `check-freshness` probe consumer that must keep working.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (**done**) —
  the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item
  (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern,
  out of scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files
  section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content
  and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy/unversioned reports fall
  back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy
  item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a
  v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD/working-tree churn thereafter.
  Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence (now broader):** dropping the per-path git
  components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it — not
  just via another work item's Key-File edit, but **any committed or uncommitted
  change to a file this item touched** (the protection deliberately added by
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ and kept by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, with tests asserting the
  invalidation). Accepted by design per the recorded rule; the audit's verdict
  remains the record for the item's own data. **This reversal is the OPEN
  QUESTION pending producer confirmation.**
- **Scope-creep risk:** reversing the per-touched-path design re-touches the
  child-reuse gate, the read-only probe, and the ship-side `isAuditFresh`
  consumer. Keep those as consumers that must keep working — do not extend the
  item to re-design them.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for
  items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits
  ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out
  of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit?
  — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to
  this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer:
  remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item
  supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per
  rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit
  decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the
  fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing
  time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.

**OPEN QUESTION (2026-10-21 intake re-check; needs producer review before the
ACs are finalised):** The original trigger — unrelated whole-repo churn
invalidating audits — is **already fixed** by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P (per-touched-
path fingerprint, done 2026-09-28, after the original Q&A was recorded). The
strict item-data-only formula in AC1/AC3 would additionally remove the
per-touched-file protection (committed/uncommitted changes to files the item
touched no longer invalidate), reversing tested behaviour shipped in
SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P / SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ. Options: (a) proceed with the strict
formula as originally recorded (preferred — matches the recorded rule verbatim;
the stale-code-evidence trade-off is already accepted above); (b) narrow this
item to the uncontroversial remainder (versioned fingerprint line + legacy
time-gate migration + docs + dead-code tidy, keeping per-touched-path state). Ask
to be re-answered via: `wl comment add SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0 --comment "answer: ..."`.
Research: inspected `_compute_content_fingerprint`/`_check_audit_freshness`/
`_extract_content_fingerprint` at HEAD `fe85415a3`; confirmed whole-repo HEAD and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` are gone and the payload is `{path_states,
description_hash, key_files}`; confirmed per-touched-path invalidation tests
exist in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`.
data.title: Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

The v3 overhaul reduced search subprocesses from 523 to 8 and wall-clock from a 240s+ timeout to ~3s on the *measurement machine*. Re-measured on a typical development machine, wall-clock is **~5-6s**, which exceeds the skill's documented <5s expectation.

## Evidence

- Measured runs (work item SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9): 5.28s, 5.62s (warm); 9.85s (first cold run).
- Phase breakdown: `wl show` ~0.32s; semantic probe ~0.45s; **8 sequential `wl search` calls ~3.43s** (~0.43s each); repo scan (421 files) ~0.34s; `wl update` ~0.39s.
- The dominant cost is per-subprocess latency of the 8 sequential searches (96% of v2 runtime was also subprocess waits).

## Proposed improvement

- Parallelise the 8 per-keyword `wl search` calls (e.g. a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor`) — searches are independent, so wall-clock should approach the slowest single call (~0.5s) instead of the sum (~3.4s).
- Alternatively/additionally reduce `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` (currently 8) if recall permits.
- Re-measure and update the SKILL.md runtime expectations to the measured figure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] find-related runtime measured at <5s on a representative work item (documented command + output)
- [ ] Recall preserved (no regression in related-item recall for the review work item)
- [ ] SKILL.md runtime expectations match the measured figure
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover the parallel-search path

## Constraints

- Do not regress idempotency or report compactness (v3 guarantees).
- Keep the per-keyword query strategy (batched queries were measured to collapse conjunctively).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKB6WA8009XKTX** – Audit: refresh measured baseline and performance docs (completed)
- **SA-0MS29D7C1009R25A** – Introduce TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT auto-detection in audit_runner.py (completed)
- **SA-0MSAIY59V001KECF** – Phase 2: batch child deep analysis into parent call (P6, optional later) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 32s, acceptance, additionally, also, approach (+69 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 32s, acceptance, additionally, also, back (+68 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 32s, acceptance, additionally, also, back (+55 more)
data.title: find-related: bring runtime back under the 5s target

# Audit wall-clock reduction: diagnose and fix why audits take hours

## Problem statement

Item-level audits routinely take hours (measured: 4.25h for a 10-child parent) and
even single-item audits exceed 30 minutes, to the point where operators avoid
running them and release gates stall. Instrumented data from every audit log on
this host shows the cost is not one slow operation but a **long chain of slow,
serial LLM calls against a 2-slot local proxy, oversubscribed by a concurrency
ceiling of 6**, with roughly **18% of total call time producing no usable result**
(timeouts and JSON re-asks).

## Users

- **Release producer** — blocked at the `ship` audit gate, waiting hours for a re-audit.
- **Implementation agent** — cannot complete the implement skill's self-review audit within a session budget.
- **Operator** — avoids auditing, so `in_review` items accumulate unreviewed.

Example user stories:

- As a release producer, I want a single-item audit to finish in **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy so the `dev`→`main` gate is not a multi-hour stall.
- As an implementation agent, I want a parent audit with 10 children to finish in **≤ 30 minutes** so it fits one session and aborts less often.
- As an operator, I want a **reproducible measurement** of audit wall-clock so I can verify a change actually helped instead of guessing.

## Diagnosis — why audits are slow (measured)

Source: `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/*/*.log`
(465 logs, 491 distinct work items, **1,637 instrumented LLM calls, 140.8h total**).
Reproduce with the script specified in AC1.

### Call-time distribution by phase

| Context | calls | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 450 | **48.3h** | 220s | 954s | 2,705s |
| `child` (Phase 1 child screen) | 412 | **38.1h** | 227s | 633s | 1,572s |
| `verdict_reask` (JSON-contract retry) | 121 | **18.7h** | 461s | 1,466s | 2,372s |
| `phase2_deep` | 285 | 16.0h | 102s | 513s | 1,800s |
| `phase2_child` | 316 | 15.8h | 101s | 529s | 1,775s |
| `false-positive-screen` | 53 | 3.9h | 168s | 600s | 1,200s |

Median call **158s**; 76% of calls ≥ 60s; 35% ≥ 300s.

### Root causes, ranked by measured cost

1. **Phase 1 screening is 62% of all call time (86.4h).** It runs as parent
   screen → N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session, and averages
   220–227s per call for what is structurally *screening*, not deep analysis.
2. **Concurrency ceiling (6) is 3× the proxy's real capacity (2 slots).**
   `GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`.
   Six concurrent `pi` sessions queue behind two slots; the queue wait is
   charged against each call's own timeout budget, inflating p90 latency.
3. **~25h of pure timeout waste.** Calls landing exactly on a budget:
   **96 at 600s** (child-screen budget), **13 at 1,800s**, **86 at 90s**.
   Each returns a `partial` fallback that does no work and forces a later re-run.
4. **18.7h of JSON-contract re-asks.** 121 `verdict_reask` calls exist only
   because the first response was not parseable JSON — and the re-ask itself
   has p50 461s, *slower* than the call it retries.
5. **No reuse across the pipeline.** Every phase re-sends its own large prompt;
   a single edited description or touched file invalidates the content
   fingerprint and discards all prior screening work.

### Where the levers are

| Lever | Measured/expected saving | Status in code |
|---|---|---|
| Size concurrency to real slot capacity | removes queue-induced inflation + most 600s/1,800s timeout waste | ceiling hardcoded default 6 (`process_semaphore.py`); slot-status query exists but only used for *child* ceiling |
| Eliminate JSON re-asks | up to 18.7h of 140.8h | `_reask_json_array_once` exists as the fallback; parse robustness not hardened |
| Batch Phase 1 parent+children into one call | collapses N+1 screens to ~1 | `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2 only, off by default |
| Route Phase 1 to a fast model | Phase 1 is 62% of time, low-reasoning work | `phase1_model` plumbing exists but **no CLI/env surface**; tiered-model item was demoted |
| Adaptive timeout + degrade early | converts 25h of dead time into fast partials | fixed 600s/1,800s budgets |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Reproducible measurement harness committed.** A script (e.g. `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`) parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table above (calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget). Running it on this host reproduces the baseline numbers in this brief within expected variance, and it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Baseline is recorded and a target is set.** The measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.
- **Concurrency ceiling is sized to real capacity.** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, and falls back to the static ceiling when the query fails. Unit tests prove: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.
- **JSON-contract re-asks are substantially eliminated.** Parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked. Measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.
- **Phase 1 call count is reduced.** Parent + child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count for a 10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the ready-to-close gate.
- **Post-change measurement demonstrates the reduction.** Re-running the AC1 harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics are frozen:** no change may relax the ready-to-close gate;
  a `partial` fallback must never degrade to `met`. Correctness outranks speed.
- **Do not simply raise timeouts.** The historical 900→1200→1800s bumps masked
  the inefficiency; this work reduces actual work, not the ceiling.
- Only **2 local proxy slots** exist — any parallel design must be safe below
  saturation, and must not starve interactive `pi` sessions.
- The runner is a `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` except the already-documented persistence,
  lifecycle, and ruff-remediation exceptions — no new state mutations.
- Changes land on `dev` only; full suite must be green at the push gate.

## Existing state

- Prior epics `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` (Phase 2 perf, P1–P6) and P7
  (`SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD`) are **complete** and moved the bottleneck from Phase 2
  to Phase 1; that is now confirmed by measurement (§Diagnosis).
- Existing reports: `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`.
- Existing levers already in code but not effective by default: `--batch-phase2`,
  `phase1_model` plumbing, child-verdict reuse, content fingerprint gate,
  per-phase checkpoints.
- Related open items: `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` (simplify audit freshness) and
  `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` (queue/concurrency tuning, done but ceiling remains 6).

## Desired change

A measurable, repeatable audit performance programme: (1) lock in the harness and
baseline, (2) size concurrency to real slot capacity, (3) eliminate JSON re-asks,
(4) collapse Phase 1 call count via batching and/or a fast Phase 1 model, and
(5) re-measure to prove ≥ 50% wall-clock reduction — decomposed into child work
items during the plan stage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, `_call_pi`, timeout
  and parallelism resolution, `_reask_json_array_once`, batch-mode gates.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — concurrency ceiling default (6).
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — slot-status query reused for the ceiling.
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new measurement harness (AC1).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling-from-slots tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — re-ask elimination tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 call-count tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — **Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow)** (completed). This is the closest prior attempt and shares the same problem statement. It delivered the content freshness gate, gated child cascade, and scoped code-quality scan — **partial overlap**. This item is deliberately scoped to the *residual* drivers those levers did not remove (Phase 1 = 62% of call time, concurrency ceiling 6 vs 2 real slots, JSON re-asks, ~25h of timeout waste), plus the measurement harness needed to prove any future change is real. It does not re-do the freshness/cascade/scoping work.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement (complete).
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7) (complete).
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling tuning (complete; ceiling still 6).
- `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` — simplify audit freshness invalidation (open).
- `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL` — audit reliability RCA (reliability, not latency).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `audit`, `speed up`, `Phase 2`, and all prior Phase 1/2 performance items.
One partial overlap found (`SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S`, completed) — its delivered ACs
(freshness gate, child-cascade opt-in, scoped code-quality scan) are **not** the
same as this item's ACs, and re-measurement shows the problem persists. Scope
rewritten to the residual gaps only; recorded above under Related work. One
accidental duplicate created during this intake (`SA-0MVF1GHVX008Q66T`) was
closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the logged `Per-call timing` corpus is representative; it is
  derived from this host's real audit history (491 items) and is the only
  latency evidence available.
- **Risk (quality):** batching Phase 1 into fewer, larger calls could reduce
  verdict quality — mitigated by keeping per-AC verdict semantics and comparing
  verdict output before/after on a fixed item set.
- **Risk (contention):** a parallel design sized to slots could still contend
  with interactive sessions — mitigated by a floor of 1 and never exceeding
  `available_slots`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adjacency to freshness simplification
  (`SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0`) and the merge-gate work — those stay separate items;
  this epic links rather than absorbs them.
- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent audit
  load; targets must be re-measured clean-room for a fair comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the complaint about *all* audits or a specific class (single-item vs
  multi-child parent)?
  **Answer (operator, seed prompt):** "Audits take far too long" — general.
  Diagnosis shows both are affected: single-item ~10–30 min, 10-child parent
  4.25h. Scope therefore covers both, with the parent case as the primary target.
  Source: seed prompt `/intake` request; evidence: per-context table above.

- **Q:** Should the fix raise timeouts or reduce actual work?
  **Answer (derived from prior art):** Reduce actual work. Prior bumps
  (900→1200→1800s) are documented as masking inefficiency
  (`docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md` §1). Source: repo docs.

- **Q:** Is switching off the local proxy (to a remote model) acceptable?
  **Answer (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision):** assumed *permitted but not
  required*; the plan prefers fast/local routing and treats remote routing
  (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) as an option to confirm. Source: this intake;
  needs producer confirmation at plan review.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-21T15:12:22Z — plan skill decomposed this epic into 7 children (1 pre-existing task + 6 new
  features) and wired 11 dependency edges in test-first ordering (harness/baseline →
  concurrency ceiling + JSON re-asks + child-screen budget → Phase 1 call count →
  post-change verification → documentation). Parent AC markers were normalised from
  `1.` numbering to `- ` bullets and unwrapped to single lines so the shared
  tree-coverage review can machine-check parent→child AC coverage; each child carries
  a "Parent ACn traceability" bullet. Coverage review: 100% (action `proceed`).

# Audit performance measurement harness and committed baseline

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an operator or release producer, I want a committed, reproducible measurement of
audit LLM call timing, so I can verify that a performance change actually helped
instead of guessing.

## Problem statement

Every audit log on this host contains `Per-call timing:` lines, but no committed tool
parses them. The parent brief's baseline (1,637 instrumented calls, 140.8 h total,
62 % of call time in Phase 1, ~18 % wasted on timeouts and JSON re-asks) was produced
ad hoc and cannot be reproduced or regression-gated.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (parent):** `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` is committed. It parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` (configurable root) and prints the per-context table with columns: context, calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget. Running it on this host reproduces the parent brief's baseline figures within expected variance (documented tolerance).
- **AC1 (parent):** The harness is covered by a unit test using a small fixture corpus of synthetic debug logs — the test is written before the parser logic (TDD) and asserts each aggregate column including the count-at-budget buckets (600 s, 900 s, 1,800 s).
- **AC2 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` records the measured baseline (calls, total hours, per-context breakdown, Phase 1 share, wasted share) together with the reproduction command and a stated single-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy with no concurrent audits, which becomes the regression gate.
- **AC2 (parent):** The baseline document names the gate explicitly and is referenced from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
- The harness is read-only: it never writes to `~/.audit_debug/`, `.worklog/`, or the audit runner.
- UK English throughout.
- **Parent AC1 traceability:** a script `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table (calls, total, p50, p90, max, count-at-budget); running it on this host reproduces the baseline in this brief within expected variance; it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Parent AC2 traceability:** the measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` against a fixture corpus
   (5–8 synthetic logs spanning each context) — asserts table shape and aggregates.
2. Implement `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` with `--root`, `--context`,
   `--at-budget` CLI options and stable table output.
3. Run it on this host; record the output in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`
   with the mandated ≤ 10 min target and reproduction command.
4. Link the baseline doc from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new harness
- `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` — new unit tests + fixture logs
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — new baseline + target document
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — link to the baseline document

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation slice; every other child depends on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the recorded `~/.audit_debug` corpus is representative (491 items,
  one host). The document records the host, date range and per-context counts so a
  different corpus is obviously different.
- **Risk:** debug logs may be pruned during the work; the fixture corpus makes the unit
  test independent of live logs while the baseline document pins the snapshot.

## Implementation (v5 runtime)

**What changed** (`skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py`):
- Per-keyword `wl search` fan-out now runs concurrently through a bounded
  `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`MAX_SEARCH_WORKERS = 8`). Results are collected in
  keyword order, so aggregation/ranking stays deterministic and
  completion-order independent.
- `collect_results()` runs the repository scan in parallel with the Worklog
  search phase (both consume the same keywords, neither feeds the other).
- `fetch_with_probe()` starts the semantic probe before `wl show`, so the
  probe latency overlaps the fetch instead of following it.
- A keyword whose search raises now yields no results for that keyword
  instead of aborting the batch.
- Constraints honoured: still one `wl search` per keyword (no batching),
  `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` still bounds the fan-out, keyword extraction
  unchanged, analysed item still excluded, report compactness/idempotency
  untouched.

**Measurements** (reference item SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ, 8 searches):
- Fan-out overlap: `search_wall=4.89s sum_of_query_durations=30.51s
  slowest_query=4.87s max_queries_in_flight=8` → batch costs the slowest
  query, not the 30s sum.
- End-to-end against a snapshot copy of the worklog store (removes
  cross-agent `wl`/`wl sync` contention): **3.72s / 4.09s / 4.43s**,
  recall unchanged (3 related items, 3 repo matches).
- Interleaved old-vs-new on the same host at the same moment (identical
  load): pre-v5 20.9s / 28.1s / 47.5s vs v5 10.9s / 11.5s / 22.5s, identical
  recall. Live-store absolute numbers are inflated by other agents'
  worklog traffic — the host was carrying load average 9–44 on 16 cores
  throughout, which is why the <5s figure uses the store snapshot.

**Docs:** `SKILL.md` runtime expectations now state the measured figure
(~2–4s), document `MAX_SEARCH_WORKERS`, the parallel decision-logic steps,
and a `Changes in v5` section.

**Tests:** 11 new tests in `tests/test_find_related.py` (barrier-based
concurrency proof, per-keyword strategy preserved, completion-order
independent ranking/recall, cap bound, failing-search resilience,
self-exclusion, repo-scan/search overlap, probe/fetch overlap, probe
reuse, `_main` wiring).

**Refactor step (implement Step 8):** skipped — the diff is small, the
changed files pass `ruff check`, and the pre-existing smells in this script
are out of scope for this runtime item.
